scenarios.name: setpoint_above_limit_light_reheat
scenarios.description: Reference vector: SAT setpoint 14 °C with 20% of zones reheating — setpoint above the low limit, nothing to report

scenarios.name: setpoint_low_but_reheat_light
scenarios.description: Reference vector: SAT setpoint 10 °C with only 30% of zones reheating — a cold setpoint the zones are not fighting, so no fault

scenarios.name: setpoint_low_with_widespread_reheat
scenarios.description: Reference vector: SAT setpoint 10 °C with 65% of zones reheating — over-cooling paid for by reheat; alarms after alarm_delay (3600 s)

scenarios.name: setpoint_exactly_at_low_limit
scenarios.description: Edge case: SAT setpoint sits exactly on sat_sp_low_limit (12 °C) with 65% of zones reheating — the strict `<` keeps it out of the alarm

scenarios.name: reheat_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Edge case: exactly half the zones reheating (0.5) against a 10 °C setpoint — the strict `>` means the fraction must exceed the threshold

scenarios.name: reheat_burst_clears_before_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: a morning reheat burst at 0.65 falls back to 0.30 at t=1800 — the condition clears inside alarm_delay, so no alarm

scenarios.name: reset_raises_setpoint_before_delay
scenarios.description: Transient: reheat stays at 0.65 but a working SAT reset walks the setpoint from 10 °C to 13.5 °C at t=1800 — the fault condition ends before it can alarm

scenarios.name: reheat_dip_restarts_persistence
scenarios.description: Transient: reheat dips to 0.40 at t=900 and returns to 0.65 at t=1200 against a 10 °C setpoint — persistence restarts from the return, so the alarm lands at 4800 s, not 3600 s
